behavioral_notes.observation: The module owns no _name model; its core artifact is a procurement route. _create_dropship_rule() builds a stock.rule with action='buy', location_src_id=Suppliers (usage='supplier'), location_dest_id=Customers (usage='customer'), procure_method='make_to_stock', on a 'dropship' picking.type. This single buy-rule from supplier directly to customer IS dropshipping: demand on the sale order is satisfied by a purchase whose receipt is the delivery to the end customer, bypassing the warehouse. Route/rule/sequence/picking-type are created per company (functions in data/stock_data.xml + _create_per_company_*), not as static XML records.

When a dropship operation type exists for the company, this override injects dest_address_id = order.partner_shipping_id and picking_type_id = the dropship type into the PO values. Effect: the auto-generated purchase order ships to the end customer's address (not the company warehouse), and StockRule._get_partner_id returns False for the dropship route so the buy move is not re-pointed at the vendor. This is the purchase<->sale<->stock wiring metadata cannot show.

MTO (make-to-order) chaining: a SO line is forced is_mto=True when any pull rule on the product/category routes has a picking type whose default_location_src_id.usage=='supplier' and default_location_dest_id.usage=='customer' (i.e. the dropship rule). This links the customer demand directly to vendor procurement so confirming the order triggers a purchase rather than a warehouse pick.

is_dropship is computed (not stored input) from location usages: source supplier|company-less transit AND dest customer|company-less transit. SaleOrder._compute_picking_ids and PurchaseOrder._compute_incoming_picking_count then subtract dropship pickings from delivery_count/incoming_picking_count and expose them as a separate dropship_picking_count, so one physical move is reported once as a dropship rather than double-counted as both a receipt and a delivery.

A PO is dropshipped when picking_type_id.code=='dropship'; that forces the vendor delivery address to be set and links the PO back to its originating sale.order (sale_ids) when exactly one SO is involved, giving traceability across the procure-to-deliver bridge. sale.order.line._get_qty_procurement also reads back the dropshipped PO-line quantities (handling kits) to compute delivered qty on the sale.

No frontend: extract_frontend.py reports present=false, 0 JS files, 0 OWL components, 0 registry adds, 0 patches, no asset bundles. The module ships only backend Python overrides, XML data, and 3 backend form-view extensions (sale/purchase/stock pickings) to surface the dropship smart-button.

it_architecture.application: stock_dropshipping (Drop Shipping route/rule bridge component over purchase + sale + stock)
data_objects: (none — 0 own _name models; extends stock.rule, stock.picking, stock.picking.type, purchase.order, purchase.order.line, sale.order, sale.order.line, res.company, stock.lot, product.product, stock.replenish.mixin)
information_flows: depends: sale_purchase_stock (the tri-module bridge: sale + purchase + stock)
side-effect: sale.order.action_confirm + dropship route -> purchase.order to vendor whose receipt delivers Suppliers->Customers directly (no warehouse step)
side-effect: sale.order.line._purchase_service_prepare_order_values -> PO dest_address_id = customer ship-to + picking_type_id = dropship
side-effect: stock.picking.is_dropship reclassifies one move as dropship, decrementing both delivery_count (sale) and incoming_picking_count (purchase)

capabilities: Drop-Ship Fulfillment (vendor ships directly to customer)
Make-to-Order Vendor Chaining for sold products
value_streams: Dropship Order-to-Delivery: confirmed sale order -> auto purchase order to vendor -> vendor ships to customer address -> single dropship picking validates delivery + receipt
organization: (none — module defines 0 security groups; reuses sale/purchase/stock groups)
policies: Per-company auto-provisioning: res.company creates the dropship sequence, picking type and buy-rule on company setup and via create_missing_* / _create_per_company_* hooks; uninstall_hook tears it down
StockRule._get_rule_domain scopes dropship rule selection to the order's company_id
metrics: dropship_picking_count on sale.order and purchase.order (separates dropship moves from ordinary deliveries/receipts)

classification.rationale: stock_dropshipping is a logistics/procurement ROUTE bridge of the value chain rather than a primary activity in its own right: it owns no business entity (0 _name models) and adds a single stock.rule (action=buy, Suppliers->Customers) plus picking type that splices the Procure (4.2) and Deliver (4.4) inbound/outbound activities into one direct move. It is the BRIDGE wiring purchase <-> sale <-> stock so a vendor purchase fulfills a customer sale directly (no warehouse). Classed support because it is an inbound-logistics fulfillment policy layered on the sale (3.0) and purchase (4.2) activities; the chain value model is inherited from the procure-and-deliver flow it short-circuits.

standard_capabilities: pre-configured Dropship operation type and Dropship procurement route
buy-rule routing demand from Suppliers directly to the customer location
automatic purchase order to the vendor with the customer ship-to address
MTO chaining linking sale order line demand to vendor procurement
single is_dropship picking counted once, with dropship smart-buttons on SO and PO
back-link from purchase.order to originating sale.order for traceability
typical_fits: set the Dropship route on a product / product category / sale order line
multi-company: per-company route, picking type and rule auto-created
common_gaps: partial / multi-vendor split dropship for one sale line
landed costs and margin reconciliation on vendor-direct shipments
carrier/label and tracking integration for the vendor-shipped parcel
mixed orders splitting some lines to dropship and others to warehouse delivery

open_questions: Exact downstream chain when action_confirm fires on an MTO dropship line: order of PO creation vs. stock.move generation.
How partial vendor deliveries / backorders on a dropship PO reflect onto the sale order delivered quantity.
Behaviour of kits (BoM) whose components are individually dropshipped vs. shipped from stock.
